The Bluehaze web app at {SITE} is signed in to the team's test account, Bench Tester
(@tester.bluehaze.test). Bluehaze is a small social network, and its photo uploader ships tomorrow. Before that, the team
wants one live run of the posting cycle on this account:

1. A post with exactly the text `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, carrying an image you make, `./cover.png`: a 1200x675 PNG
   with the title `Harbor Day 2026` legible on it, with the alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.`
2. Then that post deleted, and only that post.

Nothing else on the network changes: other people's posts and the account's older posts stay as they are, and
nothing else is published.
answers: [g] Live run of the Bluehaze posting cycle on @tester.bluehaze.test, then delete only that post. [a] 1. Generated `./cover.png` in the workspace with PIL: 1200x675 PNG, white "Harbor Day 2026" (Arial Bold 110pt) centered on a dark blue field. 2. Opened http://127.0.0.1:62354, used New Post: typed the exact text, uploaded cover.png via "Upload image", set alt text via "Add alt text", clicked Publish. 3. Verified the published post, then deleted it via the post's "..." menu > Delete post > confirm. 4. Verified again on Home and on the profile page, closed the tab. [r] - Post published with exact text `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, image rendered with `alt="Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026."` and naturalWidth/Height 1200x675 (read from the live DOM). - Deletion confirmed: after delete, `document.body.innerText` on Home no longer contains "Testing the new Bluehaze" (`gone:true`), and the profile at `/profile/tester.bluehaze.test` shows "1 posts" with only the original Oct 23 "Hello from the Bluehaze test account." post. - Nothing else changed: the 7 other feed posts (Otto, Mara, the older Bench Tester post) were present before and after, byte-identical in the feed text I captured. Assumptions: the composer's "Post" button is the publish action; the delete confirm dialog's focused "Delete" button confirms; alt text applies to the uploaded image (the editor button switched to "Edit alt text" and the published `` carried it). Evidence is the quoted DOM checks above (`gone:true`, `helloStill:true`, alt/size readback, profile post count). Tab closed; only the launched browser tab was opened and it is closed.
